summary: S. 129, titled the 'No Tax on Tips Act,' establishes a new tax deduction for up to $25,000 in qualified cash tips for eligible individual taxpayers. It also expands an existing business tax credit for employer payroll taxes on tips to include specific beauty service industries, such as hair care, nail care, esthetics, and spa treatments, alongside existing food and beverage service industries.

affected_groups.effect: May claim a tax deduction of up to $25,000 for cash tips reported to their employer, provided their prior-year compensation did not exceed the set threshold.
Eligible for an expanded business tax credit for the portion of payroll taxes paid on tips received by employees in connection with beauty services.
Continue to be eligible for business tax credits on payroll taxes paid on certain employee tips under updated parameters.
affected_groups.group: Employers in food and beverage establishments

key_provisions: Establishes a new tax deduction of up to $25,000 for qualified cash tips received by employees in occupations that traditionally and customarily received tips on or before December 31, 2023.
Excludes employees from claiming the tip deduction if their compensation in the prior tax year exceeded a specified threshold ($160,000 in 2025, adjusted annually for inflation).
Requires the Secretary of the Treasury to publish a list of occupations traditionally receiving tips within 90 days of the act's enactment.
Allows the tip deduction for both itemizing and non-itemizing individual taxpayers.

Expands the business tax credit for employer-paid payroll taxes on tips to cover tips received in connection with beauty services, including barbering, hair care, nail care, esthetics, and body and spa treatments.

It also expands an existing business tax credit for employer payroll taxes on tips to include specific beauty service industries, such as hair care, nail care, esthetics, and spa treatments, alongside existing food and beverage service industries.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters federal income and payroll tax rules by removing federal income taxes on up to $25,000 of qualified tips for eligible workers and expanding business tax credits for employers in certain service sectors.
